description: UNIVERSE is a software-led research project for the “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!” challenge. We turn NASA Earth observations into interactive trend maps and regional investigations, with traceable data provenance and transparent uncertainty. We welcome collaborators in Earth science, climate statistics, data analysis, visualization, and science communication who want to make complex Earth-system signals understandable and reproducible.
summary: UNIVERSE is a web-based Earth-system trend investigation platform built for NASA's “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!” challenge. It lets users select a location, NASA POWER variable, and historical period, then investigates daily observations through monthly quality screening, calendar-month anomaly calculation, robust Theil–Sen trend estimation, and statistical diagnostics. A companion global atlas maps NASA GISTEMP v4 temperature anomalies alongside a separately attributed NOAA GPCP precipitation product. Users can inspect grid cells, investigate regions, export CSV and JSON evidence, and trace source files through SHA-256 hashes. A synthetic False-Alarm Laboratory stress-tests statistical assumptions and exposes a calibration warning: current Hamed–Rao atlas p-values remain provisional candidates, not confirmed discoveries. UNIVERSE makes trend magnitude, data coverage, uncertainty, and methodological limitations visible so findings can be investigated and reproduced rather than accepted as automatic conclusions.
details:
Project Overview

UNIVERSE addresses the challenge of identifying, measuring, and evaluating changes in Earth's environmental systems. Instead of displaying trend lines without context, it provides an interactive investigation workflow that helps users understand what is changing, where it is changing, how quickly it is changing, and how reliable the statistical evidence is.

1. User-Directed NASA POWER Investigation

Users can select a geographic location, an environmental variable, and a historical period. UNIVERSE retrieves actual daily observations through the NASA POWER Daily Point API.

The analysis pipeline:

  • Screens monthly data coverage and excludes months below the configured 80% valid-day threshold.
  • Converts daily values into monthly means.
  • Calculates calendar-month anomalies to reduce the influence of recurring seasonal cycles.
  • Estimates trend magnitude using the robust Theil–Sen slope.
  • Applies Hamed–Rao modified Mann–Kendall diagnostics when the time series meets the required conditions.
  • Provides a seasonal Mann–Kendall cross-check, data coverage information, and methodological limitations.

2. Global Earth-System Evidence Atlas

The global atlas processes two explicitly attributed gridded datasets:

  • NASA GISS GISTEMP v4 LOTI temperature anomalies on their native 2° × 2° grid.
  • NOAA PSL GPCP monthly precipitation on its native 2.5° × 2.5° grid.

Users can explore global grid cells, investigate geographic regions, examine trend magnitudes, and export selected-cell and regional evidence in JSON and CSV formats. Source-file SHA-256 hashes provide traceability to the input data used in each published build.

3. Scientific Reliability and False-Alarm Laboratory

A major design decision is to make statistical uncertainty visible rather than presenting every significant-looking map cell as a discovery.

UNIVERSE includes a reproducible synthetic Gaussian AR(1) null-calibration experiment with 1,000 simulations in each of four autocorrelation scenarios. The current Hamed–Rao implementation did not include the nominal 5% rejection rate within the Monte Carlo interval in any of the four tested scenarios. Consequently, affected global atlas results are explicitly labelled provisional screening candidates, not confirmed discoveries. The laboratory is a stress test, not observational validation or a recalibration of real-world results.

4. Technology and Implementation

The system uses JavaScript, Python, Cloudflare Workers, Cloudflare D1, Cloudflare Queues, browser-based interactive visualization, NumPy, xarray, and netCDF4. The application provides public access to the live interface, evidence exports, reproducible source code, and statistical documentation.

Google Gemini is used for bounded research-note assistance and an optional user-started conversational voice interface. OpenAI ChatGPT assisted with software development, code review, testing, debugging, and documentation. Numerical trend estimates and statistical calculations are performed by deterministic application code, not generated by an AI model.

5. Impact and Originality

UNIVERSE aims to make Earth-system trend investigation more accessible, transparent, and reproducible. Its main contribution is combining user-directed NASA observations, global gridded evidence, robust trend estimation, uncertainty diagnostics, and an openly visible false-alarm laboratory in one working application.

The project does not claim causal attribution, independent station validation, or automatic scientific discovery. Its purpose is to help people investigate environmental signals while understanding the evidence and its limitations.
